question.latex:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I: Chromium $III$ Complexes $en = ethylene diamine$
A. $[Cr$CN$_6]^{3-}$
B. $[CrF_6]^{3-}$
C. $[Cr$H_2O$_6]^{3+}$
D. $[Cr$en$_3]^{3+}$

List - II: $\Delta_0 $\text{cm}^{-1}$$
I. $15,060$
II. $17,400$
III. $22,300$
IV. $26,600$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
question.plainText: Match List - I with List - II. List - I: Chromium III Complexes en = ethylene diamine A. [CrCN_6]^{3-} B. [CrF_6]^{3-} C. [CrH_2O_6]^{3+} D. [Cren_3]^{3+} List - II: Delta_0 text{cm}^{-1} I. 15,060 II. 17,400 III. 22,300 IV. 26,600 Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

explanation.latex:
The crystal field splitting energy ($\Delta_0$) relies heavily on the strength of the ligands according to the spectrochemical series.
The strength of the given ligands increases in the order: $F^- < H_2O < en < CN^-$.
Therefore, the splitting energy $\Delta_0$ will also follow the same order: $[CrF_6]^{3-} < [Cr(H_2O)_6]^{3+} < [Cr(en)_3]^{3+} < [Cr(CN)_6]^{3-}$.
Matching this with the numerical values:
B ($F^-$) $\rightarrow$ lowest $\Delta_0 = 15,060\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (I)
C ($H_2O$) $\rightarrow$ next $= 17,400\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (II)
D ($en$) $\rightarrow$ next $= 22,300\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (III)
A ($CN^-$) $\rightarrow$ highest $= 26,600\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (IV)
The correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

question.latex:
Which of the following complexes will show coordination isomerism?
A. $[Ag$NH_3$_2][Ag$CN$_2]$
B. $[Co$NH_3$_6][Cr$CN$_6]$
C. $[Co$NH_3$_6][Co$CN$_6]$
D. $[Fe$NH_3$_6][Co$CN$_6]$
E. $[Co$NH_3$_6][Fe$CN$_6]$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
question.unicode:
Which of the following complexes will show coordination isomerism?
A. [AgNH_3_2][AgCN_2]
B. [CoNH_3_6][CrCN_6]
C. [CoNH_3_6][CoCN_6]
D. [FeNH_3_6][CoCN_6]
E. [CoNH_3_6][FeCN_6]
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
question.plainText: Which of the following complexes will show coordination isomerism? A. [AgNH_3_2][AgCN_2] B. [CoNH_3_6][CrCN_6] C. [CoNH_3_6][CoCN_6] D. [FeNH_3_6][CoCN_6] E. [CoNH_3_6][FeCN_6] Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

explanation.latex:
Coordination isomerism arises when both the cation and anion are complex ions, and isomerism occurs due to the interchange of ligands between the two coordination spheres. Such interchange yields a distinctly new compound (salt) mostly when the central metal atoms in the complex cation and anion are different.
For B, D, and E, the central metal atoms in the cationic and anionic parts are different (Co/Cr, Fe/Co, Co/Fe). For instance, in B, exchanging ligands produces $[Cr(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]$, which is a distinct salt isomer.
For A and C, the metals are identical. Fully swapping the ligands leads to a structural representation that simply writes the new anionic complex first, which yields the exact identical chemical substance (e.g., swapping all ligands in C gives $[Co(CN)_6][Co(NH_3)_6]$, which is the same salt). Thus B, D, and E clearly exhibit coordination isomerism.

question.latex:
Match the LIST-I with LIST-II
List-I $Complex ion$
A. $[Cr$H_2O$_6]^{2+}$
B. $[Co$H_2O$_6]^{2+}$
C. $[Cu$H_2O$_6]^{2+}$
D. $[Mn$H_2O$_6]^{2+}$
List-II $Calculated spin only magnetic moment $BM$$
I. 3.87
II. 5.92
III. 4.90
IV. 1.73
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
question.plainText: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II List-I Complex ion A. [CrH_2O_6]^{2+} B. [CoH_2O_6]^{2+} C. [CuH_2O_6]^{2+} D. [MnH_2O_6]^{2+} List-II Calculated spin only magnetic moment BM I. 3.87 II. 5.92 III. 4.90 IV. 1.73 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

explanation.latex:
Water is a weak field ligand, resulting in high spin complexes.
A. $Cr^{2+}$ has $3d^4$ configuration. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 4$. $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ BM. (A -> III)
B. $Co^{2+}$ has $3d^7$ configuration. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 3$. $\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87$ BM. (B -> I)
C. $Cu^{2+}$ has $3d^9$ configuration. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 1$. $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$ BM. (C -> IV)
D. $Mn^{2+}$ has $3d^5$ configuration. Number of unpaired electrons $n = 5$. $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM. (D -> II)
Matching code: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
